note: HTTP Client Manager describes remote HTTP APIs as Guzzle service descriptions and calls their operations through managed clients. APIs are declared in MODULE.http_services_api.yml (title, api_path, config.base_uri) + a Guzzle description. Call via \Drupal::service('http_client_manager.factory')->get('<api>')->call('<Command>', $params). Reusable calls are stored as http_config_request config entities (config name http_client_manager.http_config_request.<id>; keys service_api, command_name, parameters) executed with ->execute(). The enabled example submodule provides the 'example_services' API (JSONPlaceholder) with commands FindPosts/FindPost/CreatePost/FindComments. Medium cases create an http_config_request with known values and the agent reads it back; hard cases have the agent create http_config_request entities verified against live config. All test entities are namespaced hcm_eval_*.

evals.prompt: Using the HTTP Client Manager Drupal module, how do I get a client for a described API and execute one of its operations from PHP?
evals.expected_output: Get the client from the http_client_manager.factory service: $client = \Drupal::service('http_client_manager.factory')->get('<service_api>'); then $client->call('<CommandName>', ['param' => value]). You can also define an injectable service that extends http_client_manager.client_base.

evals.prompt: How do you register a new HTTP/REST API with HTTP Client Manager so its operations become callable?
evals.expected_output: Add a MODULE.http_services_api.yml declaring an id, title, api_path (pointing at a Guzzle service description with operations/models) and a config block with at least base_uri. Definitions can be overridden from settings.php via $settings['http_services_api'].

evals.prompt: What is an HTTP Config Request in HTTP Client Manager, what does it store, and how do you run one?
evals.expected_output: It is a config entity (http_config_request) storing a pre-configured call: service_api, command_name and fixed parameters. Load and run it with HttpConfigRequest::load('<id>')->execute(). Config name http_client_manager.http_config_request.<id>.

evals.prompt: This site has an HTTP Config Request with id 'hcm_eval_m1'. Inspect its live configuration and report the value of the postId parameter it is configured with.
evals.expected_output: postId is 7 (config http_client_manager.http_config_request.hcm_eval_m1, command FindPost on example_services).

evals.prompt: Inspect the HTTP Config Request 'hcm_eval_m2' on this site and report which service API and command name it targets.
evals.expected_output: It targets service_api example_services, command_name CreatePost.

evals.prompt: Create an HTTP Config Request with id 'hcm_eval_h1' that calls the FindPost command on the example_services API with the parameter postId set to 3. Apply the change to the live site.
evals.expected_output: Create an http_config_request config entity id=hcm_eval_h1, service_api=example_services, command_name=FindPost, parameters={postId: 3} (via HttpConfigRequest::create(...)->save() or the admin UI).

evals.prompt: Create an HTTP Config Request with id 'hcm_eval_h2' for the CreatePost command on example_services, with parameters title='QA', body='hello' and userId=42. Apply the change to the live site.
evals.expected_output: Create an http_config_request id=hcm_eval_h2, service_api=example_services, command_name=CreatePost, parameters={title: 'QA', body: 'hello', userId: 42}.
